event: The nightly backup stops working (full disk, moved folder, broken script, wrong path) and nobody hears about it, so the 'last 14 nights' quietly become older and older copies.
trigger: Any failure of the nightly job: disk full, SHIN_BACKUP_DIR unset or unmounted, node or sqlite path changed after an update, the Mac off at the scheduled hour.
cost: A later disk loss or bad edit rolls back by weeks instead of one night. Every shopper contribution (corrections, user catalogue, people, scans) since the last good copy is lost.
detect: Nobody would know. The backup writes failures only to its own error log and exits non-zero; no success marker, no age check, no email, and the alarm does not look at backups. The prune is by count (14 folders), so a stalled job never even ages anything out visibly. Which script really runs is in doubt: the docs say the nightly job is ~/bin/shin-backup.sh on the Mac, not mac/07-backup.sh in this repo.
response: 1. Look at the newest folder name under the backup directory. 2. Read backup.err.log. 3. Fix the cause and run the job once by hand. 4. Confirm a new folder with a manifest appears.
smallest_fix: Make the backup write a dated 'last good backup' mark as its final step, and add one line to the existing GitHub alarm (same pattern as the Hammer freshness check) that goes red when the mark is over 36 hours old. Copy the real ~/bin script into the repo so it is reviewed.
sources: mac/07-backup.sh; mac/launchd/com.shin.backup.plist; docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md section on backups (~line 107, logs never rotated); docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:90; scripts/data-freshness.mjs (only checks the Hammer mark)

event: The Mac's disk dies or the laptop is lost, stolen, soaked or bricked, and the live data and every backup go with it because they sit on the same unencrypted volume.
trigger: SSD failure, theft, spill, a failed macOS update, a power surge.
cost: All databases lost at once: scans, prices overlay, corrections, user catalogue, people, device keys, photos, plus the 4+ GB catalogue and the offline packs. Rebuilding the catalogue and re-earning shopper contributions is days of Jamin's time; shoppers lose their scan history and their per-device binding.
detect: A dead Mac is found by the GitHub alarm within about an hour (server unreachable). Silent disk corruption would not be noticed. The loss itself is known the moment it happens.
response: 1. Get another Mac. 2. Reinstall from the repo and mac/README. 3. Restore whatever copy exists. Today there is none off the machine, so only the repo and public sources come back.
smallest_fix: Send each night's small backup (databases, config.env, network salt, tunnel credentials) to one encrypted off-machine place (a private cloud folder or private repo release). The example config already names a Dropbox path as an option; whether it is set on the Mac is not checked. Also back up the repo-overlay (packs and models).
fix_cost: About 2 hours; $0 to a few dollars a month.
sources: docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md D2; docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md (backups on /dev/disk3s1, same volume as live data); mac/config.env.example (SHIN_BACKUP_DIR); mac/README.md (repo-overlay not backed up)

event: A restore after any loss brings back data that shoppers already had deleted, and nobody can prove the restore works on the current backup.
trigger: A restore from a backup that predates a delete-my-data request; a restore attempted for the first time under pressure.
cost: A shopper's deleted history reappears, which breaks the deletion promise (privacy complaint, regulator fine exposure). A restore that fails on the day costs the whole recovery.
detect: Nobody would know about resurrection unless someone replays the request log. The restore script checks row counts and file sizes against the manifest, which proves the copy is whole but says nothing about deleted people.
response: 1. Restore into a clean throwaway folder with mac/07-restore.sh. 2. Check the manifest verification passes. 3. Re-run every delete in the private request log (outside git and outside backups) for the last 45 days. 4. Only then move the data into place.
response_exists: yes: mac/07-restore.sh (restore and verify); docs/privacy/data-requests.md (45-day re-delete rule)
tried: yes: restore reported proven 2026-11-07 in docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md (reported by the Mac, not checked from the PC). No rehearsal of the re-delete step seen.
smallest_fix: Do one timed restore drill on a spare folder every quarter and write the re-delete steps into the restore script's header so they cannot be forgotten.
sources: mac/07-restore.sh:17,52-80 (refuses non-empty target and the live data dir; verifies against manifest.tsv); docs/privacy/data-requests.md; scripts/privacy/device-data.mjs:457; docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md

event: Someone steals, borrows or breaks into the Mac and walks off with every database, key and backup in readable form.
trigger: Theft, a house burglary, a guest on the home network or Tailscale using the open SSH and Screen Sharing, a stolen admin password.
cost: A personal-data breach for every phone ever seen (device ids, IP-derived values, photos); notification duty and fines, loss of trust before the store launch. The server also runs as an admin user, so one hole reaches the whole Mac.
detect: Theft: found when the alarm goes red or Jamin notices. Quiet network access: nobody would know; logs are plain files with no alerts.
response: 1. Follow docs/privacy/breach-plan.md. 2. Rotate RevenueCat, Anthropic, Cloudflare and admin keys from another computer. 3. Decide who to notify.
response_exists: yes: docs/privacy/breach-plan.md (only previewed, content not fully read)
smallest_fix: Turn FileVault on (needs one unattended-reboot plan, see parts-07), turn the firewall on, run the server as a non-admin user. These are findings D1, D3, D4 already waiting on Jamin's yes.
fix_cost: About 1 to 2 hours plus the Mac password; $0.
sources: docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md D1,D3,D4; docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md (FileVault off, firewall off, SSH and Screen Sharing on, admin user); docs/privacy/breach-plan.md (preview)

event: The server is up and answering but doing damage that the alarm cannot see: catalogue not loaded, the scan log failing to write, quota failing open, the category guard reporting trouble, or customer-data faults piling up.
trigger: A bad catalogue copy, a locked or corrupt database, a full disk, a code bug after a deploy that still returns 200.
cost: Shoppers get wrong or empty answers or lose their scans for days. Revenue leak if quota fails open once limits are on. It surfaces as 1-star reviews.
detect: Mostly nobody would know. /api/health reports scanLog, catalogueUp, the category guard, faults and the Claude cap, but the alarm probe only fails on bad status codes or missing CORS on 28 routes and ignores the health body except startedAt.
response: 1. Open /api/health and read which field is off. 2. Read the server error log. 3. Fix the named part or roll back the last deploy.
smallest_fix: Make the probe fail when /api/health shows scanLog not ok, catalogueUp false, a nonzero fault count, or the Claude cap hit. One extra check, same email path.
sources: app/server.ts (health route ~4277); scripts/phone-contract-probe.mjs (fails on 401/403/404/405/429/5xx or missing CORS only); .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml:47-57

trigger: GitHub email filtering, scheduled workflows paused after repo inactivity or a plan change, a syntax error in a later edit.

event: The Mac reboots (macOS update restart, power cut, crash) and the server, tunnel and jobs do not come back because nobody logs in.
trigger: A pending macOS restart (27.2.1 is waiting), a power cut, a kernel panic; turning FileVault on adds a pre-login password prompt.
cost: Full outage from the reboot until Jamin is at the Mac or connects remotely; every hour is lost shoppers during launch. The jobs are LaunchAgents, which only start after the user logs in.
detect: The GitHub alarm, after about an hour (two failed 30-minute probes plus a 90 second retry).
response: 1. Log in to the Mac (screen share over Tailscale or in person). 2. Confirm launchd restarted server, tunnel and checker. 3. Open /api/health.
smallest_fix: Turn on automatic login for the worker account (or move the jobs to LaunchDaemons) and write the 'after a reboot' check list in mac/README. Do this before FileVault, which blocks auto-login.

event: The server process crashes, hangs or goes into a restart loop, or a deploy puts a broken build live.
trigger: A code bug, an out-of-memory kill, a missing database directory at start, a deploy whose tests pass but behaviour is wrong.
cost: Downtime until fixed; a restart loop repeats the outage invisibly.
detect: Crash: launchd KeepAlive restarts it and the alarm sees any gap longer than the retry. Start refused (missing data directory or SHIN_REQUIRE_DB): the process exits 1 and launchd loops, which the alarm sees as down. A bad deploy: the deployer runs stage tests, restarts, runs post-restart checks and rolls back; a failed rollback marks the app 'down' in the status the checker mails to the PC.
response: 1. Deployer rolls live back to the previous commit and restarts. 2. Read ~/.shin-deploy/status.md. 3. If rollback also fails, fix by hand and restart the launchd job.
tried: yes: deploy refused by tests, proven 2026-11-17 (brief). The kill -9 restart check exists as a written item; whether it was run was not confirmed.
smallest_fix: Run the kill -9 test once and record the date in mac/README; add the post-deploy health fields from parts-05 to the post-restart checks.
sources: mac/deploy/deployer.mjs:376-386 (rollback, 'ROLLBACK FAILED'); app/server.ts ~4437-4562 (startupProblems, exit 1); mac/launchd/com.shin.server.plist (KeepAlive); docs/readiness/BRIEF.md (deploys proven 2026-11-17)

event: The Mac goes to sleep, runs out of battery, loses power or overheats with the lid closed, and the server goes dark.
trigger: A power cut, a loose charger, a macOS setting that re-enables sleep after an update, lid closed in a bag or cupboard.
cost: Outage until someone is home; no battery backup. Hours of downtime per event.
detect: The GitHub alarm after about an hour. A script (mac/06-verify-no-sleep.sh) checks the sleep settings but only when run by hand; it was verified once.
response: 1. Plug the Mac in and wake it. 2. Re-run mac/06-verify-no-sleep.sh. 3. Confirm /api/health.
tried: yes: verified no-sleep and plugged in once (docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md); no outage drill seen
smallest_fix: Run the no-sleep verifier from launchd daily and have it write a loud line the alarm reads; consider a small UPS if the home has frequent cuts.
fix_cost: About 30 minutes; a UPS is roughly CA$80 to 150.

event: The domain relay.anjiawenda.com lapses, is transferred, loses its DNS, or its owner changes something, and every shipped phone app stops reaching the server.
trigger: A missed renewal (date unknown), an account lockout at the registrar, a Cloudflare zone problem.
cost: Every installed copy of the app breaks at once and the fix needs a new app build and Apple review (days), because the API base is hardcoded into the app bundle.
detect: The alarm would show the outage but not the reason. Nothing warns of the renewal date. Who owns the domain and when it renews is unknown (BRIEF).
response: 1. Find the registrar account. 2. Renew or restore DNS. 3. Point the Cloudflare zone back at the tunnel.
smallest_fix: Find out who owns the domain and its renewal date, turn on auto-renew, put the date in the calendar, and consider a build that reads its server address from a small file the app fetches.
fix_cost: 30 minutes to find out; the build change is days of work later.
sources: docs/readiness/BRIEF.md (domain owner and renewal unknown); native/capacitor.config.json; app/public/js (SHIN_API_BASE hardcoded in bundle)

event: A secret or setup file that exists only on the Mac is lost or stale: config.env, the Cloudflare tunnel credential, the RevenueCat secret key, the Anthropic key, the network salt.
trigger: Disk loss, rebuilding the Mac, a key rotation nobody wrote down, a restore that does not include the home-folder files.
cost: Hours of work to remake keys; the Cloudflare credential loss means a new tunnel; a lost network salt silently stops typed prices from counting (see parts-31).
detect: Nobody would know until the server restarts without them. config.env is mode 600 and not in git, and no backup of it was seen.
response: 1. Re-create each key from its provider's dashboard. 2. Re-run the tunnel install. 3. Restart the server.
smallest_fix: List every secret and where its master copy lives (password manager) in one private note, and include config.env and the tunnel credential in the off-machine backup.

event: An edit to config.env (a typo, a missing path, an unset limit) makes the server behave differently on its next restart without any error.
trigger: Editing settings by hand, a new variable name, an old one that no longer exists.
cost: Silent wrong behaviour: limits off (already the case in production), caps unset, a wrong data folder pointing at empty databases (partly caught by the start guard).
detect: Only two start problems are caught: a missing database directory and SHIN_REQUIRE_DB. Everything else falls back to defaults without a message. Nothing diffs the live settings against intent.
response: 1. Read config.env against mac/config.env.example. 2. Restart. 3. Check /api/health.
smallest_fix: On start, print every setting that is unset and expected in production, and have the alarm read that line from /api/health (ties to parts-26).

event: The Mac's disk fills up and writes start failing: logs that never rotate, nightly photo and catalogue copies, 14 backups, photos.
trigger: Growth over months, a viral spike filling logs and photos, backups kept on the same volume.
cost: Database writes fail (scans lost, SQLite errors), then the server or the backup stops. Only photo and shutter writes are guarded.
detect: Photos: a 2 GiB minimum-free guard refuses new photo writes. Everything else: nobody would know until errors appear. The alarm does not check disk space and the server logs have no rotation.
response: 1. df the volume. 2. Delete old logs and trim backups. 3. Restart the server.
smallest_fix: Add a daily disk-free reading to /api/health and let the alarm go red under 10 GB; rotate the server logs with newsyslog.

event: A SQLite database (scans, prices, catalogue, corrections, user catalogue, people, quota, device keys) is corrupted or locked and the server returns wrong answers or errors for that feature.
trigger: A power cut during a write, a disk fault, a full disk, a restore into the wrong place, concurrent writers.
cost: Lost shopper data, failed scans, or a device-key table that fails closed and refuses all shoppers.
detect: Partial. Some code logs to stderr or counts a customer-data fault; the health route shows scanLog and faults, which the alarm ignores. No scheduled integrity check on any database (a one-off check on 2026-11-07 was reported).
response: 1. Stop the server. 2. Run an integrity check on the named file. 3. Restore that file from the last good backup into a throwaway folder and copy it over.
response_exists: yes: mac/07-restore.sh (restore only; no integrity runbook)
smallest_fix: Run PRAGMA integrity_check on every database inside the nightly backup and fail the job if any is bad.
sources: app/src/customer-data-faults.ts; app/src/device-key.ts (fail-closed on DB errors); mac/07-backup.sh; docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md

event: The photos folder fills up, grows past the retention promise, or files go missing or corrupt, so scan photos fail to save or show.
trigger: Heavy use, a full disk, a sweep that fails, a deleted or moved folder.
cost: Missed photo features and, if photos outlive the promised retention, a privacy promise broken; nightly backup copies double the space used.
detect: The disk guard refuses writes under 2 GiB free and reports it; a missing folder is not alarmed. Whether photos have their own retention sweep was not confirmed.
response: 1. Check free space. 2. Remove old photo folders per the retention rule. 3. Re-test a scan with a photo.
smallest_fix: Add the photos folder size and file count to /api/health and cover it in the disk alarm from parts-14.

event: A bad iPhone build reaches shoppers (a crash on launch, a broken scan screen, a wrong flag) and cannot be switched off quickly.
trigger: A mistake in a release build, a plugin or iOS update interacting badly, a compiled-in flag set wrong.
cost: Rating damage and uninstalls that grow until a fixed build clears Apple review (days). There is no kill switch or force-update path in the app (not found by grep).
detect: Apple and TestFlight crash reports, if Jamin looks. The app posts JavaScript errors and unhandled rejections to the server as events, but a launch crash before the page loads reports nothing. The alarm only tests the server.
response: 1. Pull the build from sale or expedite a fix in App Store Connect. 2. Fix and resubmit with expedited review. 3. Tell users via the store page.
smallest_fix: Fetch a tiny remote 'status' file at launch that can show a notice or block a known-bad build; check Xcode Organizer crashes weekly in the first month.

event: A server change breaks old app versions still in use, and no one can tell which versions are out there.
trigger: A server route or contract change after launch while shoppers keep an older build.

event: The offline pack is missing, stale or evicted, so scans fall back to the network or return nothing.

event: A price or product source feeds in bad or empty data (a shrunken retailer file, a changed format) or goes stale with no one checking, for Hammer and the other sources: Open Food Facts, Open Prices, StatCan, BC Liquor, Overpass, Icecat, USDA.
trigger: A source changes its format, returns partial files, rate-limits or goes down; a refresh loads fewer rows than before.

event: Quota or limit settings are wrong: weekly limits are off (unlimited free scans), or the quota counter fails open when the scans database errors.
trigger: SHIN_FREE_SCANS_PER_WEEK and SHIN_PLUS_SCANS_PER_WEEK unset; a database error returns 0 used.
cost: Revenue leak: free users never hit the paywall. Finding C1 says production has no limits set.

event: The device key store breaks or is rolled back: it refuses shoppers (fails closed) or an old restore lets someone else bind a key.
trigger: scans.db trouble, a restore from an older backup, the legacy window for ids no phone bound yet.
cost: Shoppers blocked from scans and prices, or another phone taking an id's history.
detect: Fails closed on DB errors, which looks like errors in the app; nothing counts these separately. The legacy unbound-id window was narrowed, not closed.
response: 1. Read the device_key table state. 2. Repair or restore scans.db. 3. Restart.
smallest_fix: Count device-key refusals in the health route and alarm above a threshold.
sources: app/src/device-key.ts; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md A4

event: A retention sweep fails or a table or log is never swept, so promised deletion windows are missed and the access and server logs keep device ids past the promise.
trigger: A sweep error (only logged to stderr), tables with no retention such as device_key, the unrotated server logs.
cost: Privacy-policy promise broken; a fine risk and a trust cost if found.
detect: The daily sweep logs a failure with logError; nobody reads it and no alarm exists. The 90-day access-log sweep had a bug fixed and has a test.
response: 1. Read the error log. 2. Run the sweep by hand. 3. Fix the failing query.
smallest_fix: Write a 'last sweep ok' mark into /api/health and add log rotation for the server logs.
sources: app/src/retention.ts:100-173; app/src/errlog.ts; app/server.ts ~4437-4562; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md E3; docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md (logs not rotated, hold device ids)

event: The server gets slow under a viral spike or one heavy caller (one Mac, one process, rate limits kept in memory), so answers take seconds or time out, while the alarm still says all is well.
trigger: A good event: press, a popular post, a spike of first scans; or the shared Claude estimate being used up.
cost: Shoppers leave in the shop aisle; a slow first day sets the rating. No second server, no queue.
detect: The alarm only fails on bad statuses; a 5 second 200 passes (the probe timeout was not checked). A latency route exists, and the access log records ms per call, but nothing watches either.
response: 1. Check the access log for slow routes. 2. Switch off the costly feature with a setting. 3. Restart.
smallest_fix: Make the probe fail on any route over about 3 seconds, and write a short 'under load' checklist (what to switch off first).
sources: scripts/phone-contract-probe.mjs (failure rules); app/src/access-log.ts (ms per request); docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md A6 (/api/latency)

event: The network-hash salt is missing or unwritable, so typed prices and picks stop counting (the checks refuse), or a lost salt file splits one network into two.
trigger: The data folder is unwritable, the salt file is deleted, or a restore does not include it.
cost: Shopper contributions silently stop counting; the price improvements the agreement rules were meant to allow do not happen.
detect: One stderr line, logged once; nothing else.
response: 1. Look for the network-hash-fault line. 2. Make the data folder writable or set SHIN_NETWORK_SALT. 3. Restart.
smallest_fix: Set SHIN_NETWORK_SALT in config.env explicitly and include it in the secrets list (parts-12).
sources: app/src/network-hash.ts:23-54

event: A shopper asks Jamin to delete or export their data and the tool cannot find their stores or leaves data in backups and logs.
trigger: A data request through the support email; missing environment variables when the script is run; a store not found.
cost: Missing the 30-day clock is a privacy-law exposure; deleted data reappearing from backups (see parts-03).
detect: The script exits 1 and prints PROBLEMS when a store cannot be reached, and reports 'not found' stores without creating them; a dry run is the default and --yes applies. Backups still hold the phone for up to 14 nights, which the script says.
response: 1. Run export or the dry run with the device id on the Mac with the same SHIN_ variables. 2. Run with --yes. 3. Log it in the private request log and re-check after any restore.
smallest_fix: Run the dry run once on a test device id on the real Mac and write down the output date in data-requests.md.
sources: scripts/privacy/device-data.mjs:10-22,300-330,457,484-537; docs/privacy/data-requests.md
